meta.title: Aleix Casas — Full Stack Software Engineer
meta.description: Full Stack Software Engineer in Barcelona. I build and operate systems that have to hold up: Python/Django over PostgreSQL, Angular front ends, LLM features in production, and Kubernetes on GCP.

hero.intro: I build and operate systems that have to hold up. Three years in the product team of a SaaS analytics platform: Django REST APIs over PostgreSQL holding tens of millions of records, an embeddable widget platform and an AI feature with its cost under control, both in production. MSc in Software Development & Architecture, La Salle (URL), 2026, where I took a Kubernetes event pipeline from 80 to 5,000 events per second.

about.title: About me
paragraphs: I work in a team of three, which means I own what I ship: the design decisions, the delivery and the consequences. It taught me early that the interesting part of a feature is rarely the code — it's the schema underneath it and what happens when the data grows.

Most of my time goes into backend and data: Django REST APIs, PostgreSQL, query plans, indexes and moving expensive work off the critical path. The other part is the front end — Angular, and the migration of a whole codebase to signal-based reactivity. Recently I've spent it on the parts that only show up under load — connection pooling, backpressure, autoscaling that does what you think it does — and on getting an LLM to do something genuinely useful inside a product.

I've just finished an MSc in Software Development & Architecture at La Salle (URL). I'm interested in systems that have to hold up: data design, performance, and decisions that still make sense two years later.

jobs.summary: IDDIGO, a SaaS urban analytics platform tracking over 1,000 performance indicators for cities and territories. I work in a product team of three engineers, which means owning what I ship end to end.
points: Designed the embeddable widget platform: any feature of the Angular app can be configured and embedded in client websites, with a single entry point, route guards, its own JWT authentication and a per-client Content Security Policy enforced at the Nginx layer. Live in production.

Led the AI diagnosis project on Google Gemini from proposal to production and delivered the MVP in one month: structured context, asynchronous generation with Celery, per-institution quotas and a daily spend limit, and versioned reports with user ratings.
Migrated the frontend to Angular 20 and signal-based state in a 650-file change that removed over 5,000 lines net, and rebuilt frontend testing from scratch with Vitest and Playwright.
Django REST APIs over PostgreSQL holding tens of millions of records; cut the heaviest endpoints from several seconds to under one through query and index optimisation.
Mentored two junior developers through code review, pairing and technical growth plans.

projects.title: Projects
projects.intro: Most of what I build lives behind a login or belongs to a client, so these are written up as case studies rather than repository links: what the problem was, what I decided, and what came out of it.

items.name: Vista Flota
items.imageAlt: Vista Flota operator dashboard showing 2,500 trucks on a live map with fleet KPIs
items.summary: A real-time IoT fleet platform: a device on each truck publishes telemetry over MQTT — position, speed, fuel — which the platform ingests, deduplicates and turns into live fleet state, trips and alerts on an operator dashboard, archiving the full history for route reconstruction.
highlights: The requirement was 1,000 events/s sustained with zero message loss. The baseline architecture died of OOM at 80.

Removed bottlenecks one at a time — measure, diagnose, fix, re-validate — with Prometheus and Grafana: deduplication moved out of PostgreSQL into Redis, PgBouncer multiplexing 200 client connections over 20 real ones, watermark-based backpressure, MQTT QoS 1, and KEDA replaced by HPA once profiling proved the pods were CPU-bound.
Final result: 5,000 events/s at peak, 3,200 sustained, 0.00% loss.
items.note: Team project across three areas (Application, Infrastructure, IoT). I owned the Application area. Repository is private.

items.name: Embeddable widget platform
items.tagline: Any feature of the product, inside someone else's website
items.summary: Clients wanted parts of IDDIGO inside their own websites. Rather than a one-off embed, I treated it as an architecture problem: how to let any feature of the Angular application be shared as a widget, configured for each client, and kept closed off from the rest of the product.
highlights: A single entry point loads each widget's configuration from its ID, and route guards keep visitors inside the functionality that widget allows.
Widget visitors aren't platform users, so they get their own JWT authentication with proactive token refresh, running alongside the platform's existing authentication.

Embedding is limited to each client's allowed domains: Nginx asks the backend for each widget's allowed origins and builds the Content Security Policy from them. Violations are logged and reported to Sentry.
Later extended with territory pages configurable per widget and custom typography per client. Live in production.

items.name: AI diagnosis with Gemini
items.tagline: A written analysis of every indicator, with the cost under control
items.summary: IDDIGO tracks over 1,000 indicators per territory, but interpreting the tables and charts took time and technical knowledge. I led the project as owner, from proposal to production, and delivered the MVP in one month: a tab on every indicator page that writes an analysis of trends, anomalies and territorial comparisons.
highlights: The context sent to Gemini is built in five blocks (territory, indicator metadata, historical series, breakdowns and comparable territories) by a pure function with its own tests.
Generation runs asynchronously in Celery, with a global daily spend limit and a daily quota per institution. Cache hits don't count against the quota.

Reports are cached for 30 days and only reused while the underlying data hasn't changed. Regenerating creates a new version, so every user rating stays tied to the exact text that was read, and the token usage of each call is recorded.
The model's output is treated as untrusted: rendered as Markdown through Angular's sanitizer in the app, and with its HTML escaped in the PDF export.
